text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Friday it assigned a triple-B-minus rating on Owens-Illinois Inc's proposed $250 million offering of senior notes due 2004 and $250 million senior notes due 2007.
Owens-Illinois has a strong presence in the worldwide packaging market and its financial condition is improving, Duff & Phelps said.
But the credit rating agency also said its rating reflects the company's aggressive growth strategy and the risks associated with ongoing, but declining, asbestos litigation.

Owens-Illinois' proposed refinancing plan is favorable, Duff & Phelps said. The plan would reduce interest expense and long-term debt, extend debt maturities, reduce the debt-to-capital ratio and improve the company's financial flexibility, the rating agency said.

Owens-Illinois' pro forma debt-to-capital would fall to 73 percent from 79 percent after taking into account the refinancing plan and the company's recent decision to acquire AVIR SpA, Italy's largest maker of glass containers.

"While further improvement in credit protection measures is anticipated, DCR believes the company will continue to seek debt-financed acquisition opportunities, particularly of international glass and plastics packaging companies, limiting upside ratings potential," Duff & Phelps said.
The credit rating agency also reaffirmed a rating of triple-B-minus for the company's senior debentures and a double-B rating on Owens-Illinois' senior subordinated notes.
